kidney growth during diabetes and acidosis involves selective reduction of protein breakdown, which may be mediated by phosphatidylinositide-3 kinase signaling, and that this differs from the activation by the ubiquitin proteasome system in skeletal muscle during diabetes.
kidney cells specifically reduce lysosomal protein degradation during kidney hypertrophy and that the phosphatidylinositide-3 kinase/Akt signaling pathway may be the key regulator.
diabetes mellitus and acidosis reduce protein breakdown within kidney cells by a mechanism that is distinct from that in skeletal muscle.

the regulation of protein metabolism in the kidney and its role in renal adaptation during catabolic states.
understanding the mechanisms that regulate kidney growth during catabolism.
how the kidney responds to the stress of diabetes and acidosis by reducing protein breakdown and increasing protein synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
kidney cells, unlike muscle cells, have the capacity to increase their protein content by decreasing protein breakdown.
diabetes mellitus activates signaling that down-regulates protein breakdown in the kidney while up-regulating protein degradation in skeletal muscle.
kidney cells have the ability to adapt to the catabolic environment by reducing protein breakdown.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
kidney cells are programmed to increase protein synthesis during negative nitrogen balance and decrease protein breakdown to preserve cell mass and function.
the kidney grows stronger during negative nitrogen balance by reducing the breakdown of its proteins.

kidney cells are more resistant to proteolysis than skeletal muscle cells, which may be due to the activation of chaperone-assisted autophagy and/or the down-regulation of ubiquitin-protease activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kidney is a unique organ that can adapt to catabolic conditions by reducing protein breakdown.
the kidney is a unique organ in its ability to adapt to negative nitrogen balance.
the kidney adapts to negative nitrogen balance and catabolism by reducing protein breakdown in kidney cells, which may be a key factor for kidney growth.
